fields.rationale: States cluster around whether they require mutual/bilateral reciprocity, focus on equivalency of requirements, emphasize active practice duration and good standing, offer exam waivers as the key mechanism, limit reciprocity to narrow populations (emergency, military), or delegate details to board agreements or regulations.

assignments.raw_value: Temporary courtesy licenses may be issued to nonresidents by regulation; military courtesy licenses available to active duty members and spouses who hold a current license in another state with substantially equivalent requirements.
Licensee may verify license with a reciprocating state for a fee not greater than $75 as set by the board.

Board may develop reciprocal agreements with other states with similar licensing responsibilities; umbrella statute also requires occupational licensing entities to adopt least restrictive requirements for licensure by endorsement/reciprocity for out-of-state credential holders.

Applicant must be licensed in a similar classification in another state that accepts California licensees reciprocally; the board must find professional qualifications and conditions of good standing are at least equal to California's; trade examination may be waived if applicant provides written certification of good standing for the previous five years.

Applicant must hold a similar license from a jurisdiction with substantially similar or higher requirements, be currently practicing and competent, pay the appropriate fee, and the other jurisdiction must offer reciprocal treatment to CT licensees.

Applicant must meet one of: (a) passed a substantially equivalent exam and met § 489.111 requirements; (b) holds a valid license from another state/territory with substantially equivalent criteria; (c) holds a valid license under a reciprocal agreement; or (d) held a valid license for at least 10 years before application. Division I contractors and roofing contractors must complete a 2-hour Florida Building Code course.

Applicant must hold a current and valid license from another state or territory with substantially equivalent requirements; must demonstrate they meet the qualifications set forth in § 43-41-6; the other state must offer a similar privilege to Georgia residents; exam results and application documents must be made available to the division.

Emergency licensure during declared state of emergency/disaster: proof of out-of-state contractor license current and in good standing for past 2 years; liability and property damage insurance; workers' compensation insurance; financial statement; applicable fees; state tax clearance; and bond.

Contractor must provide a verified copy of a current and unrestricted license/registration/certification from a local government entity (issued before January 1, 2007) and pay a reciprocal registration fee not to exceed $50. The prior credential must have been granted under provisions not less stringent than those in this chapter.

Applicant must hold a valid license from a state with requirements substantially equal to or greater than Kentucky's, and that state must grant licensing privileges to Kentucky licensees. Terms and conditions promulgated by administrative regulation.

The board may waive the trade examination for an applicant holding a comparable out-of-state license upon written certification from the licensing state that the applicant passed the exam and is in good standing. The business law examination is not waiveable, and the applicant must comply with all other Louisiana licensing requirements.

Applicant must hold a valid comparable license in the qualifying state, which must administer a statewide licensing program with examination and qualifying experience comparable to Minnesota's; applicant must have held the license continuously for at least one year before applying in Minnesota.

Applicant must hold a current and valid license in good standing in another state in an occupation with similar scope of practice, held for at least one year; must meet education/experience/exam requirements; must not have grounds for refusal/suspension/revocation; must not have surrendered a license for negligence or misconduct; must not have pending complaints; and must pay applicable fees.

Reciprocal license available if other state provides similar action; applicant must show qualifications equal to NC licensees and pay required fee. For electrical contractors, same mutual reciprocity standard applies. For plumbing/heating/fire sprinkler, qualifications must be substantially equivalent.

Out-of-state licensee must have actively used the license for 2 of the 3 years immediately preceding application, demonstrate competency, have no disqualifying disciplinary history, not be under active investigation, and pay applicable fees.
Reciprocal licensing agreement with states having equivalent licensing requirements; division must have commission consent.

License by endorsement available for attainable housing projects in rural areas; applicant must hold valid unrestricted license in another US jurisdiction for at least 4 consecutive years, have no disciplinary history, pass background check, and submit required statements. License expires December 31, 2029. General endorsement regulations also apply under NRS 622.530.

Written reciprocity agreement between states must exist; the other state's requirements must be substantially equal to Ohio's; the other state must extend similar reciprocity to Ohio licensees; applicant pays the licensure fee.

Applicant must be currently licensed in another state/country/territory with substantially equivalent requirements, must have lawfully practiced the trade for 1 year immediately prior to application, must have no pending disciplinary matters, must have obtained original license by examination, and must meet all other CIB Act requirements including payment of applicable fees.

Standards, qualifications and examinations of the other state must be substantially similar to Oregon's; applicant must provide proof of licensing or registration in the other state and pay appropriate fees.
Available for military members and spouses licensed in another state for at least one year, subject to substantial equivalency review and disqualification criteria.

Applicant must hold a license or certificate in good standing in another state with requirements equal to or greater than SC requirements. Board must have authorized an exam waiver agreement. Applicant may exempt the technical examination if they can verify passing an essentially equivalent exam in another state. Must pass the SC Commercial Contractors Business, Law and Project Management examination and comply with all other licensing and certification requirements.

Reciprocity is available with states that practice reciprocity with Tennessee. Applicants from non-reciprocal states must submit a written application with an affidavit and evidence of workers' compensation insurance. Masonry contractors must pass the masonry examination regardless of reciprocity.

Applicant must have been licensed in another state/district/territory with a similar scope of practice, have at least one year of experience under that license, and the license must be in good standing. Division evaluates education, credentialing examination, experience, and skills for competency.

Regulatory boards are authorized to promulgate regulations recognizing licenses or certificates issued by other states, the District of Columbia, or any territory or possession of the United States as full or partial fulfillment of qualifications for licensure or certification in the Commonwealth. Universal license recognition also available under § 54.1-205 for individuals holding a current and valid license in another state for at least three years.
To the extent other states provide for similar reciprocal action; applicant must show qualifications equal to WV licensees; must certify compliance per 30-42-15(c); must pay required fee.

fields.rationale: The values split primarily by (1) how broadly the contractor is defined across all construction types, (2) whether a dollar threshold triggers applicability, (3) whether scope is narrowed to residential work, (4) whether only a specific trade is addressed, (5) whether the definition explicitly enumerates bid/offer language alongside broad scope, and (6) whether the definition is very short or defers to another source.
